articles.title: SHIPPING ON TIME ISN'T ENOUGH
articles.summary:
Your IT teams deliver projects on time. But does the work solve the right problems? A project mindset focuses on scope, deadlines, and delivery. A product mindset starts with customer problems and business outcomes.

This guide shows how IT teams can work more like product teams—prioritize the right problems, learn before they build, and connect each sprint to a business result.

articles.title: AUTONOMY AND INNOVATION
articles.summary: Incumbents will adopt AI cautiously because they have more to lose from mistakes. Startups can embrace autonomy more aggressively, giving them a natural advantage in turning AI into disruption.

articles.title: INSIDE PM AT STRIPE: WHAT COMES AFTER "BECOME A BUILDER?" (61 MINUTE VIDEO)
articles.summary: AI is pushing every product-building role upstream rather than simply eliminating functions. PMs will increasingly create leverage through shared context, judgment, strategy, persuasion, and domain expertise while AI and adjacent functions absorb more execution.

articles.title: THE DEADLINE THAT WAS ALREADY MISSED
articles.summary: Bad roadmaps often fail from missing dependencies, not bad estimates. Working backwards exposes what must be true before execution begins.

articles.title: A GOOD MOVE IS ENABLING
articles.summary: Good product moves create value now while opening better options for what comes next. Teams should avoid short-term wins that lead to strategic dead ends.

articles.title: FIGR AI GENERATES HIGH FIDELITY DEPLOYMENT READY SCREENS
articles.summary: Making a screen is easy. Getting UX right in an existing product takes context. Figr learns your design system, guidelines, flows, and analytics first. (SEE HOW THAT CONTEXT SHAPED UX ACROSS GLOBAL PRODUCTS [11]). Then you can map states, test edge cases, write PRDs, and export to Figma with Auto Layout, components, tokens intact.

articles.title: START YOUR NEXT FLOW IN FIGR →
PRODUCT OWNER INTERVIEW QUESTIONS FOR THE AGE OF AI
articles.summary: As AI lowers the cost of building software, product judgment matters more than tool fluency. Great Product Owners know what to build, what to stop, and where AI should assist rather than decide.

articles.title: TO INVENT WAYMO, THEY HAD TO REINVENT PM (60 MINUTE VIDEO)
articles.summary: Waymo shows how PM must evolve for problems without clear metrics or playbooks. The key is defining what good looks like, setting concrete checkpoints, and building teams capable of learning their way forward.

articles.title: BIG-BANG REDESIGNS VS. LEGACY MODERNIZATION
articles.summary: Big-bang legacy redesigns often fail because critical dependencies are easy to miss. Modernizing gradually, with users involved and workflows replaced in small slices, reduces risk and delivers value sooner.

articles.title: THE ORACLE PROBLEM: AN INVISIBLE BOTTLENECK TO AI AND MEDICINE
articles.summary: Healthcare AI benchmarks can measure test performance without proving clinical effectiveness. Better evaluations must measure whether AI improves real-world health outcomes.

articles.title: DEVELOPERS MUST BECOME MINI-PMS
articles.summary: AI is pushing engineers beyond code and toward greater product ownership.

articles.title: ENTERPRISE AI'S BIGGEST OPPORTUNITIES
articles.summary: These opportunities lie between the model and the workflow.
